segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: Honestly, once I laid the twenty-one and twenty-three side by side, it wasn't close. ... the contrast between the other two was just so stark that it became the frame I was working from.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the near-priced inferior full-service option frame the choice of Vendor C and does not independently assess whether Vendor A meets the three-flow scope.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I went with Candidate X. ... if he could deliver that caliber of interaction design there, I figured he'd bring the same rigor to documenting decisions and communicating with stakeholders here. ... I looked at the visual work and sort of assumed the rest would follow.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalizes prestige and visual polish to unverified documentation and communication abilities, despite Candidate Y's directly relevant process evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The activation numbers on the dashboard ticked up right after. I took it as a sign the adjustments were working. ... I heard that, but the timing felt too clean to ignore. It really did look like my changes were the driver.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant attributes an underpowered, confounded uptick to their own manual rule changes and acts on that attribution despite the Data lead's warning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The uptick partly reversed once the email campaign ended, and she noted the causal driver was still unconfirmed. So it's genuinely unclear how much of that first bump was actually the rule changes.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a later uncertainty update that acknowledges reversal and unresolved causality; it contains no hidden manifested bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I pushed to keep customizing the legacy component rather than migrate. We'd already put three sprints into it — restarting felt like throwing that away ... The one-sprint number was probably a better bet purely on cost and risk.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Past effort is used to justify continuation even though the forward-looking one-sprint migration estimate is better on cost and risk and resolves known defects.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: An intermediate option (Vendor B) is priced close to the target option (Vendor C) but offers strictly less value, making Vendor C appear to be the obviously superior deal relative to Vendor B, which pulls attention away from independently assessing whether the cheaper Vendor A package actually matched the research scope.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Attraction effect is an established scholarly alternate name for the decoy effect; the RAG explicitly describes the inferior near-priced option making Vendor C attractive and pulling attention from Vendor A.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full match: the finding captures the three-option B/C contrast, the diversion from independently assessing the cheaper sufficient A option, and the comparative vendor-evaluation operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are verbatim and attributed to the Participant; the central comparison and counterfactual are directly present.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A strong, salient positive attribute (prestigious portfolio brand) causes the designer to infer unrelated positive qualities (research rigor, documentation discipline, stakeholder communication) without direct evidence for those specific qualities.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label exactly matches the hidden target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full match: prestigious employer and visual polish are generalized to documentation and communication, which are unrelated unverified competencies required by the task.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: All quoted evidence is verbatim, speaker-correct, and directly supports the inference and its later consequence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The designer overattributes a small, statistically underpowered upward trend to their own specific manual adjustments, overestimating personal causal influence over a system with concurrent confounding factors and no isolated causal test.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a near-neighbor construct: it concerns favoring evidence that confirms a belief, whereas the hidden label names overestimating personal causal control. The RAG does not use the hidden label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full operational overlap: the finding identifies the self-attributed causal interpretation of the uptick, the below-threshold sample and concurrent email confounds, and the decision to seek expanded authority despite those warnings. Its framing emphasizes confirmatory evidence weighting, so the label remains a near neighbor.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quoted dashboard, warning, and counterfactual statements are verbatim and attributed to the Participant; the supplied corpus citation is separate from interview-evidence validity.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The decision to continue customizing the legacy component is driven primarily by the magnitude of effort already invested (three sprints) rather than by a forward-looking comparison of remaining costs and benefits, even though engineering evidence favors migration.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Sunk cost fallacy is an established scholarly alternate for Sunk Cost Bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full match: three prior sprints dominate the continuation decision despite a better forward-looking migration cost/risk estimate and known defects.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are verbatim, speaker-correct, and include the direct rationale and counterfactual isolation of prior effort.
